articles.title: Tyreek Hill finds time for fans during trial and social media has plenty to say
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill is facing a civil trial over allegations of domestic abuse, but a brief interaction with fans inside the courtroom has become another talking point surrounding the former Miami Dolphins wide receiver.
articles.body:
Tyreek Hill is facing a civil trial over allegations of domestic abuse, but a brief interaction with fans inside the courtroom has become another talking point surrounding the former Miami Dolphins wide receiver.

A video circulating online appears to show Hill posing for pictures with fans during a break in the proceedings, prompting mixed reactions on social media.

While some users brushed off the moment by pointing out that Hill is involved in a civil case rather than a criminal trial for murder, others questioned the optics of a professional athlete taking photos with supporters while facing serious allegations.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders wins over ‘blind date’ interviewer with his charm
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders may still be waiting for his biggest opportunity with the Cleveland Browns, but the young quarterback is generating buzz for a different reason: his apparent chemistry with an interviewer during a playful blind-date segment. Sanders, the son of Pro Football Hall of Famer Deion Sanders, appeared on Cosmopolitan’s “Blind Date” series, where he sat down with the magazine’s editor-in-chief, Willa Bennett, for a conversation about relationships, confidence and life beyond football. The encounter produced a memorable moment when Bennett praised the quarterback's charm and asked whether he would agree to another date.

articles.title: Robert Griffin III announces plans to leave retirement and return to the NFL, with teams already showing interest
articles.standfirst: The 36-year-old insists he could operate in any offense despite not playing professionally since 2020
articles.summary: The 36-year-old insists he could operate in any offense despite not playing professionally since 2020
articles.body:
Six years away from the NFL have done little to diminish Robert Griffin III 's confidence in his ability to play quarterback, and the former Offensive Rookie of the Year believes a return could still become reality. Now working as a FOX Sports analyst, Griffin has spent years studying the league from a different perspective - and he believes that experience has helped him develop the knowledge he lacked during his playing career.

The 36-year-old revealed that he has discussed a potential comeback with NFL teams, although he stopped short of identifying the organizations involved, and offered an emphatic answer that suggested he has few concerns about adapting to the modern game. "Any of them," Griffin said to the Dan Patrick Show. "Yeah. I mean, right now, at this point in my life, with the amount of film I’ve had to watch, with the amount of growth I’ve made, you know, understanding the game, what the game needs, what you can’t do, what you have to do. Yeah, I can play in any system." His confidence comes from the extensive film study required for his broadcasting responsibilities, which he believes has sharpened his ability to recognize defenses and understand offensive concepts. However, he is not prepared to abandon a successful media career simply to generate attention or pursue an opportunity that does not make sense. "I’m not going to sacrifice that just to try to make headlines," Griffin added. "I can still throw a football and read a defense and have fun doing it, Dan. If they want me to go do it, they’ve got to, you know, I guess, pony up and make that happen." His comments follow repeated suggestions that he would consider returning, including a recent social media post claiming his daughters wanted to watch him play football again.

Griffin’s injuries transformed one of the NFL's brightest careers

Griffin entered professional football with enormous expectations after winning the 2011 Heisman Trophy at the Baylor Bears in the NCAA , before being selected second overall in the 2012 NFL Draft behind Andrew Luck . His spectacular rookie campaign with the Washington Redskins earned him Offensive Rookie of the Year honors, establishing him as one of the league's most exciting young quarterbacks. However, a serious knee injury during a playoff defeat against the Seattle Seahawks marked the beginning of a difficult period that significantly altered his career and effectively ended it. Further setbacks followed before the quarterback eventually joined the Cleveland Browns and later became a backup with the Baltimore Ravens , where he made his final NFL appearance in 2020. Griffin has previously questioned why struggling teams have overlooked experienced quarterbacks, arguing that veterans can provide stability when injuries disrupt a team's plans and has also showed an interest in representing the United States in flag football at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics . Although Griffin says conversations with NFL organizations have taken place, there has been no confirmation of a formal offer or an agreement with any team.

articles.title: Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes praise Kenneth Walker III and spark MVP conversation
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs superstars Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes praised running back Kenneth Walker III as the early MVP conversations begin regarding the running back who has already won the prize at the last Super Bowl. The fifth-year veteran, who played for the Seattle Seahawks and was the key player to beat the Patriots at the championship game, makes the games easier for the Chiefs offense and elevates Kansas City to title contender status. The sky’s the limit for Walker and the franchise eager to win another Lombardi Trophy.

articles.title: Who will perform at the Eagles vs. Jaguars halftime show in London?
articles.standfirst: The NFL Week 5 matchup will feature live music. Here's what time the game starts and where to watch it.
articles.summary: The NFL Week 5 matchup will feature live music. Here's what time the game starts and where to watch it.
articles.body:
Tomorrow is NFL Sunday, and the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars are ready for their London showdown. Their matchup at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will be one of the highlights of Week 5 , but this time, the attention won't be solely on the field. The game will also feature a musical performance bringing Afrobeats to the NFL's international stage.

How are the Eagles and Jaguars entering the London game?

The Jacksonville Jaguars have plenty of reasons to feel confident about their start to the season . With a 3-1 record and first place in the AFC South, the team is coming off a 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals and will look for another victory to maintain its position.

For Philadelphia, the outlook is different. The Eagles enter the matchup with a 2-2 record and two consecutive losses, a situation made more challenging by the injuries sidelining running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith . Both are key pieces of the offense, meaning Philadelphia will have to take on the game without them.

Ayra Starr will headline the halftime show

Now, for the music: Nigerian singer Ayra Starr will take center stage, making history as the first African artist to headline a halftime show during the NFL's International Games series.

If you're not familiar with her music yet, start with Rush and Bloody Samaritan, two of her best-known songs. You can also check out Santa, her collaboration with Rvssian and Rauw Alejandro .

What time does Eagles vs. Jaguars start, and where can you watch it?

Kickoff is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET. Here are the start times by U.S. time zone:

Central Time (CT): 8:30 a.m.

Mountain Time (MT): 7:30 a.m.

Pacific Time (PT): 6:30 a.m.

Eastern Time (ET): 9:30 a.m.

The game will air on NFL Network and stream on NFL+ .

articles.title: Travis Kelce erupts with childhood friends as Guardians complete historic comeback
articles.summary: Travis Kelce used the Chiefs’ bye week to return home for the Cleveland Guardians’ winner-take-all Game 5 against the Chicago White Sox.
articles.body:
Travis Kelce used the Chiefs’ bye week to return home for the Cleveland Guardians’ winner-take-all Game 5 against the Chicago White Sox.

Wearing a José Ramírez jersey, the Cleveland native and Guardians minority owner jumped from his seat and celebrated wildly with his childhood friends after Ramírez hit the decisive two-run home run.

Cleveland won 2-0 and completed an extraordinary comeback after losing the first two games of the series at home. Taylor Swift was not spotted at Progressive Field, but Kelce had plenty of company as his hometown team secured its place in the American League Championship Series.

articles.title: Robert Griffin III on Arch Manning: “He needs to return to college for another year”
articles.standfirst: The former NFL quarterback believes the Texas player still needs more experience before making the jump to the professional level.
articles.summary: The former NFL quarterback believes the Texas player still needs more experience before making the jump to the professional level.
articles.body:
The future of Arch Manning is already one of the biggest debates in college football. The Texas quarterback is one of the names coming up in the early conversations ahead of the 2027 Draft , but Robert Griffin III believes he is not yet ready to make the jump to the NFL.

The former Washington Commanders quarterback and 2011 Heisman Trophy winner was clear when speaking about Manning’s future. “Arch Manning should absolutely come back for another year of college football. He needs more starts and more experience before going to the NFL” , Griffin wrote on X after Texas’ loss to Oklahoma.

RG3 believes Manning still needs experience

Griffin had already defended that position a few days earlier, during an appearance on The Herd alongside Colin Cowherd. For the former player, there is a sign that lets you know when a quarterback is ready for the NFL: college football starts to seem easy to him.

“I think he should come back another year. When players are ready to go to the NFL, college football seems easy to them. For Arch, it still doesn’t seem easy,” Griffin explained. As a reference, he mentioned his own experience and Andrew Luck’s, two quarterbacks who left college after seasons in which they clearly dominated the game.

Griffin's criticism is not related to Manning's talent. On the contrary, he believes his abilities are evident. His argument is based on experience and the need to accumulate more repetitions before facing NFL defenses.

Manning arrived at Texas as one of the top recruits of his generation and spent his first seasons as Quinn Ewers' backup. In 2024, he made two starts before becoming the Longhorns' starting quarterback in 2025.

They also question his reading speed

GR3's opinion is not the only one that focuses on Manning's development. David Pollack also recently pointed out a specific aspect of his game: the speed at which he processes defenses.

“Arch Manning has exceptional talent” , Pollack explained on The Dan Patrick Show. However, he considered that his processing “is consistently a step slow” and pointed out that the quarterback still needs more repetitions to gain consistency.

Manning has shown during his time at Texas that he has the physical tools to play in the NFL, as well as the ability to create plays when the offensive structure breaks down. The question, for Griffin and other analysts, is whether he already has the consistency needed to face the next level.

Will Arch Manning stay at Texas?

"The decision is still in the quarterback's hands. Manning has another season of eligibility and could remain at Texas in 2027 before entering the Draft.

"The possibility gained even more momentum after the loss to Oklahoma. Manning threw three touchdown passes, but suffered two interceptions in the fourth quarter . One of them was returned 42 yards for a touchdown by Peyton Bowen, and the other came in the final seconds, a turnover that allowed Oklahoma to set up the game-winning field goal. The Sooners ultimately prevailed 27-24.

For Griffin, those kinds of situations reinforce his argument: Manning has the talent to make it to the NFL, but he still needs to prove that he can control the most demanding college football games from start to finish.

For now, the quarterback will have to decide whether he feels ready to take the next step or whether he prefers to stay one more year in Texas to continue developing.

articles.title: Jason Kelce gets a brutal rugby welcome in London, then fights back like a legend
articles.standfirst: The former NFL center received a crash course in rugby fundamentals from Joe Marler, the former England international
articles.summary: The former NFL center received a crash course in rugby fundamentals from Joe Marler, the former England international
articles.body:
Jason Kelce spent 13 NFL seasons battling defensive linemen. In London, the former Philadelphia Eagles center discovered that rugby comes with its own learning curve. Kelce, 38, made a surprise grassroots rugby union debut with Old Streetonians , playing approximately 30 minutes in a training match against local rivals Hackney RFC at Hackney Marshes . The retired Super Bowl champion was in the United Kingdom to cover the Eagles' matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars for ESPN , but found time to try a sport that shares American football's physical demands while requiring a different set of skills.

His introduction was memorable. Kelce was knocked flat by a hand-off early in the session, then bounced back later to power through a tackle. The appearance, part of the content he was filming for his YouTube channel, gave the former NFL star a chance to experience rugby from the inside.

Joe Marler and Ilona Maher prepare Kelce for rugby

Kelce did not step onto the pitch without preparation. Before joining Old Streetonians , he received a crash course in rugby fundamentals from Joe Marler, the former England international and Harlequins prop. He also sought advice from Ilona Maher, one of the most recognizable figures in American rugby. The guidance was important.

Although rugby and American football share tackling, blocking and an oval ball, their rules and techniques differ considerably. Rugby players wear less protective equipment, must adapt to continuous play and cannot rely on the same pauses between downs that structure an NFL game . Kelce's experience as a center gave him a useful foundation, but rugby required him to adjust to unfamiliar movements, positioning and decision-making.

A rugby welcome at Hackney Marshes

Playing in a role resembling a number eight, Kelce took on the responsibilities of a forward expected to carry the ball and contribute to the physical contest around possession. The early hand-off sent him to the ground, providing a quick lesson in rugby's tackling techniques. He recovered and later drove through a tackle, showing flashes of the strength that made him an accomplished NFL offensive lineman.

Kelce was joined by Beau Allen , his former Eagles teammate and fellow Super Bowl champion. Their presence added an NFL connection to the local matchup, but the session was ultimately an opportunity to learn rather than compete at an elite level.

For Old Streetonians and Hackney RFC, the training match brought an unexpected visitor to a local rivalry. For Kelce , it was a chance to experience a new sport without the pressure of having to master it immediately.

Kelce's London trip extends beyond the NFL

Kelce's rugby appearance came during a visit centered on t he NFL's international schedule. The Eagles' game against the Jaguars was part of the league's London Games, which have helped expand American football's presence in the United Kingdom.

Since retiring, Kelce has moved into broadcasting with ESPN while continuing to connect with fans through his podcast and digital content. The rugby session offered a different kind of access, taking him away from the analyst's desk and into an unfamiliar sporting environment.

It also highlighted the connections between the two games. American football and rugby have distinct rules and traditions, but both rely on teamwork, tactical awareness and players willing to put themselves into demanding situations for their teammates. Kelce spent his entire 13-season NFL career with Philadelphia, becoming one of the league's premier centers and helping the Eagles win Super Bowl LII . Since retiring, he has remained a prominent voice in football.

His rugby debut was never about launching a second professional career. Instead, it gave him a chance to learn from experienced players, take on a new challenge and share the experience with his audience.

articles.title: Terry Bradshaw's anxiety over the possibility of losing his job on NFL Sunday: “It's my life”
articles.standfirst: The veteran pundit was facing pressure from fans to leave his post with FOX Sports
articles.summary: The veteran pundit was facing pressure from fans to leave his post with FOX Sports
articles.body:
Terry Bradshaw has secured his future on FOX Sports for two more years, but the NFL analyst has admitted that the possibility of losing his job has made him nervous for the first time in his broadcasting career. The 78-year-old, who won four Super Bowls with the Pittsburgh Steelers , signed a multi-year contract extension that will keep him on the network through its next Super Bowl broadcast.

The former quarterback also acknowledged the challenges of remaining relevant in a business increasingly shaped by younger personalities but made it clear that he has no intention of stepping away voluntarily. “I love my job,” Bradshaw told the Los Angeles Times. “This year was the first year that I got nervous. I wanted to extend my contract. So, I signed through the Super Bowl. Two more years. I’ll be 80. “Everybody in any business has to go. The young guys are coming. But I want to be relevant. I want to be good. I want to continue on. I want America to [tune in] and watch me. I want them to [like] me.”

Bradshaw's fear of life without FOX Sports' NFL Sunday

Bradshaw 's commitment comes despite criticism of his on-air performances in recent seasons as he has faced scrutiny over mispronounced player names, confusion surrounding team changes and getting sidetracked. During FOX 's coverage in the 2026 NFL season, Bradshaw also called for the New England Patriots to drop Drake Maye over brief poor form, despite him having had led his team to the Super Bowl just months earlier. Nevertheless, Bradshaw remains determined to continue working for as long as the network wants him. His current extension takes him through the 2028-29 season, when FOX is scheduled to broadcast the Super Bowl . And the Hall of Famer had described previously described how the prospect of being unable to work on Sundays as his biggest fear, underlining just how central broadcasting has become to his life. “I think my biggest fear, if I have a fear, is not being able to work at FOX NFL Sunday. It is my life,” Bradshaw said. “It's all I've ever done. It's what I listen, you get up and go to work; are you happiest? You can't wait to get to work. Are you that thrilled? That's why I am. “Can you imagine going to work on Sunday with Strahan, Howie Long, Gronkowski, Kurt Menefee? Talk football, and to 6 million viewers out there, the number one rated show every year for the last 32 years, and have fun and enjoy and never get upset, never get jealous. “You're pulling for everybody. paragraphs: Terry Bradshaw has secured his future on FOX Sports for two more years, but the NFL analyst has admitted that the possibility of losing his job has made him nervous for the first time in his broadcasting career. The 78-year-old, who won four Super Bowls with the Pittsburgh Steelers , signed a multi-year contract extension that will keep him on the network through its next Super Bowl broadcast.

The former quarterback also acknowledged the challenges of remaining relevant in a business increasingly shaped by younger personalities but made it clear that he has no intention of stepping away voluntarily. “I love my job,” Bradshaw told the Los Angeles Times. “This year was the first year that I got nervous. I wanted to extend my contract. So, I signed through the Super Bowl. Two more years. I’ll be 80. “Everybody in any business has to go. The young guys are coming. But I want to be relevant. I want to be good. I want to continue on. I want America to [tune in] and watch me. I want them to [like] me.”
Bradshaw's fear of life without FOX Sports' NFL Sunday

Bradshaw 's commitment comes despite criticism of his on-air performances in recent seasons as he has faced scrutiny over mispronounced player names, confusion surrounding team changes and getting sidetracked. During FOX 's coverage in the 2026 NFL season, Bradshaw also called for the New England Patriots to drop Drake Maye over brief poor form, despite him having had led his team to the Super Bowl just months earlier. Nevertheless, Bradshaw remains determined to continue working for as long as the network wants him. His current extension takes him through the 2028-29 season, when FOX is scheduled to broadcast the Super Bowl .
